title: Unconscious Hunting
subtitle: At any given time, somewhere, somehow, someone is dreaming.

trails.title: Arcanist Observer Journal
trails.description: The results reflect the opinion of the majority—but does truth belong instead with the few?

content.text:
In a recent report, Paris was named the most preferred city for arcanists seeking residence. Respondents note that living in a metropolis dominated by humans is no easy feat—arcane skills, whether deliberate or incidental, often disrupt established social norms, inevitably creating confusion and conflict. Yet Paris, long known for its inclusivity toward people of many diverse backgrounds and traditions, stands apart. Parisian salons have come to regard arcane skills as a kind of marvelous and romantic art, and arcanists are frequently welcomed as guests of honor. To humans, Paris is a cradle of art; to arcanists, a haven of creativity.
Reports indicate that several renowned arcane product entrepreneurs have opened new branches in Paris this year, their trust in the city drawing increased attention. The historic capital continues to attract arcanum talent and resources from across Europe. While human concerns about the spread of arcanum persist, many believe that more cities will soon follow in Paris's footsteps.

—Arcanist Observer Journal

items.text: Interrogation Room, Vigiles Bureau

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: The Tavernier curse—every member of your family is destined to hunt endlessly for treasure until they meet their end. Passed through blood relation, usually to the relative closest to them.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: You don't believe in this so-called curse, do you, Ms. Tavernier? Or should I call you Brume?
The interview room is coldly silent except the faint whir of the recording camera.
Every word of the young woman's statement is captured by the microphone, preserved as cold signals on magnetic tape.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Given how things have turned out, it isn't as easy as a yes or no, don't you think?
She gives a helpless smile, looking down at her palms.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: But say it is true, then what of it? We're all going to die, no? One day I'll die searching for treasure, but before then, I'll live as I see fit.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: I don't plan on wasting away my days in fear.
She pauses briefly.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: The ending may be written, but that doesn't mean I want to follow the story word for word.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: That's what I told Cici as we were driving to her place. And now, looking back ... Maybe that's when it all began.
Célia's Home

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Mmm, so good! This gratin is the best. How'd you get so much flavor out of a simple potato?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: You like it, then? It's just ordinary home cooking, really. Maybe it's finally time you started doing it yourself.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Well, Papa didn't exactly teach me much in the art. He'd just pop open a tin can and say, "Be grateful. When you're in the jungle, this is a luxury."

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But he never took me to the jungle. He never even let me leave Paris. I still haven't been anywhere.
Célia smiles and shakes her head. She grabs the empty plate to scoop her friend another serving of potatoes.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: You can only blame yourself, Adèle. You were the one adamant about not becoming a hunter.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Of course! Because I don't want my life planned out like a stage play! A-And don't pretend you didn't have a part in this. You're the one who picked the page number in the advertisements.
Célia can't argue, so she pours two more spoonfuls of stew over the mash, stacking it high into a little mountain and sliding it in front of Adèle.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Sharp as ever. Since we're on the subject, how is work going? Any interesting fares lately?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Hmm. There was one thing. Not sure if I would call it interesting, though. Peculiar, perhaps?
She bites down on her spoon, trying to recall the scene from earlier. The diviner's expression is still vivid in her mind.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I was at a diviner's salon, and the host ... I don't know; I think she was trying to scam me.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: She started rambling about all these strange things that would happen, things that sounded a lot like the Tavernier Curse. And then, she, well, she died.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Died?
Célia's eyes widen, her fork clinking unconsciously against the plate.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Then the police came, and I suppose the case is still under investigation. Anyway, you know what I think of those diviners. They're not exactly people you should take seriously.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Then why were you there?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Not by choice, that's for certain. One of my clients was interested. Madame Félicienne.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: She always gets these sudden whims and insists on having everything done just as she pleases. I wouldn't have crashed my car if she hadn't—Bah, forget it. How's university life?
Célia doesn't answer Adèle's question. Instead, she catches on to her words.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: She is a long-term client, then? Can't say you've mentioned her before. Or maybe I've been spending too much time on campus, haven't I?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What do you think? I swear, this little one might forget you completely if you spend any more time hidden away in your books!

items.speaker: Feufeu
items.text: Rarr!
The tiny creature on Adèle's shoulder lets out something like a protest, prompting Célia to playfully pat its head.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Oh, heheh. I know better than that. This sweet little thing was summoned by your family's incantation. As long as you remember, he remembers.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Such a fascinating creature, the Tutelary. He sees every corner of your psyche, memory, and sensation, even your unconscious thoughts.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Hah, here comes Cici with another one of her academic lectures. Is this what you're studying these days?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Professor Roseau has found new inspiration in a Swiss psychologist's theories. He's pushing for some new breakthrough; the whole research team's working on it. We've already seen some early progress.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: That ... "collecting brain" thing?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Collective unconscious!
She adjusts her glasses with academic rigor and opens her notebook. Her poor student senses trouble.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Okay, okay. I won't forget it again.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Says the one who invents a new name for it every time. But it's even more complex than you think, Adèle, and very important. It may even help us make Paris a better city.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Imagine the minds of people like islands, each floating on their own,

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: and the collective unconscious as the water that links them all.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: This is Jung's idea of the collective unconscious—a psychic space shared by all of humanity.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Human aggression—whether it be war, class conflict, or tensions between humans and arcanists—has always been a constant.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: It's like the tides affecting the shared ocean between us. We build on our islands, but inevitably the tide will reclaim them.
The eager scholar closes her notes, fixing Adèle with an expectant look, waiting for her response.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Maybe this guy's onto something. We're all fighting for our place in these troubled times. But I don't understand what's unconscious about it. Are you saying that, deep down, we're all war-hungry maniacs?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Certainly not! But we are all under the influence of this collective mind. That's why the same conflicts happen again and again, in all times, in all places, and to all people.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: We can't force back the tide, but what if we found a new way to change the ocean itself—fill it with a new nature? One of peace and equality.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Even one tiny drop of new thought could make a world of difference.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: What we're trying to do is find some way to practically influence the collective unconscious—to create real and lasting change for everyone.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: I believe, truly, I believe it could do more to save us than any law or reform ever could!
Adèle scratches her head. She has no such lofty ambitions, nor any intention of changing anyone.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: So, you want to control everyone's minds?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: What? No! We still want people to think for themselves. We just want to change how they think.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: If we can plant a more hopeful vision into the collective unconscious, we could sow the seeds for a better future for all.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Like how Victor Hugo wrote his dreams into his books, and they reached every reader in France.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Only we're doing it in a more controlled, systematic way than simply telling stories.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What about Vincent? He seems the furthest thing from controlled. Eh, loyalty to "the Emperor" aside.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Are you sure this research is safe?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Truthfully, I wouldn't say it's entirely without risk.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: The collective unconscious is a sea of primordial images formed into cultural motifs and symbols. The more popular that symbol is—or, the more often a theme occurs across cultures—the more powerful it's said to be in our collective unconscious.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Take Napoleon, our "conquering hero-king" and cultural symbol. Vincent ... Well, he's always admired him, so perhaps that made him more susceptible.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: We're working in the mind, so it's understandable that there might be some unforeseen effects. I fear Vincent may not be the last to suffer like this until we find a safer way to proceed.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Popular symbols ... Recurring themes ... Mental distress ...
Adèle pauses as a thought strikes her.

items.speaker: Madame Raymond
items.text: They have awakened from their centuries-long slumber, bringing torment upon us! We have called them forth. We have set loose this horror ...

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Like the Beasts of Gévaudan?
She repeats what she heard back at the divination salon.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: That old legend? But why would the Beasts of Gévaudan be ...

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Wait, you might actually be onto something.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: As the rumors about the beasts have spread, it has gained a new identity in our collective unconsciousness, planting the seeds of terror inside just about everyone.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Formidable!
Her friend leaps up from the table, dives for her notebook, and starts scribbling frantically.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Thank you, Adèle! You truly are my very own academic muse! I must take another visit to the Dance of Death mural. It may play a part in all of this.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: I'll buy you one of those good-luck necklaces when I publish my paper!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Then you'd better make sure it's chic. I'll want to wear it every day.
When it comes to her research, her friend's enthusiasm is irrepressible. Adèle has long since grown used to it.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: So, what comes next?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: It's only a thought for now—one I must keep to myself. But you'll be the first to know when it's confirmed.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: I swear, you and indeed the whole world will be shocked!

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: You know—and please don't laugh—sometimes, I feel like an adventurer too. Hunting for hidden treasures with my pen and paper.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: I suppose what I do isn't all too different from your parents after all.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Forgive me, Adèle. That-that was inconsiderate of me. I got carried away.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You can find better role models than my parents, Célia.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I got another letter from them the other day. It's always the same: a mine sure to bring amazing profits and something about a mural.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: So you do read their letters! They sound exciting, don't you think? You know how much I love adventure stories.
Her friend's sudden burst of energy makes Adèle both amused and helpless.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: That you do. Sometimes, I think you're more of a Tavernier than I'll ever be.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Haha. I suppose I have always thought of you as a sister. Anyway, enough about that. Where are you taking your client tomorrow?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: To Rue de la Paix. There's a crystal parlor we're going to visit.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Because of what that diviner told you? You must be the master of your own will, Adèle. Don't let your subconscious make all the decisions.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Whatever you say, Madame Professor.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: I mean it! So many things in life are stirred up from the depths of our minds.
There's never an end to the things old friends have to say. They talk until the stars have claimed the night sky.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Cici, tell me, do you really think there's such a thing as fate?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Cici? Célia?
Her friend drifts off to sleep, wandering into some dream not yet connected to Adèle's in that sea of collective unconscious.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Well then. Good night, dear friend. May tomorrow bring good luck to both of us.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: And it was on the following day that you paid a visit to Beryl Bouanich's Parlor of Crystals?

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Correct.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: And there, you had another, ah, what did you call it? Unusual divination?

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Beryl Bouanich had foreseen my visit long before I arrived.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Just as she had foreseen all that came afterward.
